TextBlock.Text: THEATRE Ceram Sea
DATE 18 November 2028 · 0920 local
SIDE People's Liberation Army Navy
WINDOW 80 min, closes at 120
J-15 carrier fighter. Photo supplied by the SEST author
"Saying so, unfortunately, does not make it true; and if true, saying so does not always make it believed."
- Thomas C. Schelling

CERAM SEA, 0920. Two Japanese escorts came south past the Talaud Islands two days ago and are crossing the Ceram Sea this morning for the Kai Islands, where the coalition's next convoy is forming. Fleet headquarters wants their names before they join it: which ships they are, and which of them hunts submarines.

SEA EAR 31, the enclave detachment's Y-9, has the look from the east. FLYING SHARK 81 and 82, J-15s the carrier air wing has released to the enclave field, keep it company. The two ships are eighty-five miles west of the aircraft, steaming south-east for the passage east of Seram.

Expect a JASDF F-2A pair up from Langgur, the detachment that flew against the northern element's ships yesterday, to see the Y-9 off. They will be at weapons Tight, and so are yours. If they fire, you may reply against the aircraft that fired and nothing else - by direct order: fighters left free will go for the ships, and that ends the operation. Nothing afloat is a target.
Classify both escorts, then take SEA EAR 31 back east towards the field. A Misool fishing boat and a coaster bound for Sorong are in the same water.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.
Fleet headquarters
COMMANDER'S INTENT

The convoy forming at Kai sails the day after tomorrow with whatever escort reaches it, and two Japanese ships are on their way. Headquarters wants them named before they get there: which ships, and what they hunt with. Japan is at sea under its own rules, and yesterday those rules sent the Langgur fighters against northern ships south of Seram. They were not this group's ships, and the group is not at war with Japan. The same fighters will come up to see the Y-9 off. Let them. Ours are there so that seeing it off is all they do.
• Classify both Japanese escorts, then take Sea Ear 31 back east
• Fire on nothing afloat
• Bring Sea Ear 31 home
• Classify the Japanese fighters
• Harm no fishing boat or coaster

Sea Ear 31, a Y-9, and two J-15s, Flying Shark 81 and 82, out of the enclave field. Opposing: two Japanese escorts at weapons Hold, and a JASDF F-2A pair from Langgur at weapons Tight. Neutral: a fishing boat and a coaster.

The planned window is 80 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 40 minutes more; the operation is closed at 120 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
